thread:
sam: Hey team — hitting a weird intermittent issue in the browser SDK when streaming. On slow connections the client sometimes emits the final token first, then a few seconds later the middle chunks show up. No obvious error, stream stays open. :thinking:
ingrid: ugh. do you have a tiny repro or logs? can you paste the request headers and any chunk sequence ids? :eyes:
sam: minimal repro below. using EventSource -> handling `message` events. sometimes order is 1,3,4,2. super inconsistent.
```js
const es = new EventSource('/v1/stream?model=test');
es.onmessage = e => console.log('chunk', e.data.slice(0,40));
```
logs:
```
[12:01:02] chunk-id=1 payload="Hello"
[12:01:03] chunk-id=3 payload="world"
[12:01:04] chunk-id=4 payload="!"
[12:01:06] chunk-id=2 payload=", this is"
```
raj: hmm, could be a proxy or client-side reorder during reconnect. if the client reconnects and the server replays cached fragments, they might interleave. are you using last-event-id or resume tokens?
andrea: we saw proxy buffering cause reordering when chunk boundaries align with HTTP/2 data frames. the load-balancer will flush frames differently under congestion. recommended: include a monotonic sequence header in each event and the SDK should reorder before emitting to user code. also check auto-retry/backoff — if multiple parallel connections are opened briefly it can cause duplicates or reorders.
sam: interesting — i'm not using last-event-id. the SDK's autoconnect logic does backoff but i think it opens a fresh connection while old one is still draining.
ingrid: can you try toggling `enableAutoReconnect: false` in the SDK to see if it stops? also try setting `reconnectDelayMs` higher.
sam: quick test with autoReconnect=false — looks much better, no mid-chunk arrivals so far. will dig deeper. thanks. :relieved:
raj: long-term fix: SDK should expose an option to dedupe and reorder by `x-chunk-seq` header or an internal seq field if present. also emit a diagnostic metric when duplicate seq or out-of-order detected so we can trigger alerts.
andrea: agree. on the server/runtime side we can add `X-Chunk-Seq` and `X-Stream-Session` headers and make the runtime include them on every flush. then SDKs can be safe even across reconnections.
devx-bot: created issue #4601: "browser-sdk: handle out-of-order SSE fragments and provide reorder/dedupe option" — linking: https://git.redwood/infra/issues/4601 :robot_face:
ingsrid: tiny nit: please include a short failing test in sampleapp showing the proxy case (e.g., throttle to 120kb/s and force H2 frame splits) so QA can reproduce.
sam: will add repro + test. i'll paste a tiny curl chain that simulates frame-split using `nghttp` later. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
